segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Yeah, thanks for making time, Dana. I wanted to confirm the final scope before I send the order form over. I have 42 standard seats and 6 admin seats, annual term starting March 1, total at $48,600. Does that match what you have?

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: That matches. The only thing is we may add two more standard seats in April, but we don't want to hold up the March 1 go-live for that.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Totally. We can start with the 42 and 6, and if you add those two later, it's just prorated through the same February 28 end date.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Okay, good. On billing, can you split the invoice by department? Finance asked for 70 percent to operations and 30 percent to customer support.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Yes, that's fine. It'll still be one contract, but the billing tool can generate two invoice lines with those allocations. Payment terms are net 30, same as the draft we reviewed.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Net 30 works. And implementation is still the week of February 12?

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Right. Kickoff on February 12, configuration sessions on the 14th and 15th, and then user training on February 22. That gives us a few business days before March 1 if anything needs adjusting.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Sounds good. Legal had one comment on auto-renewal. They want 60 days' notice instead of 90.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: I saw that. Deal desk approved 60 days this morning, so I'll include that version in the order form.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Great. Send it to me and copy our controller, Miguel. If we get it today, I can route it for signature tomorrow.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Will do. I'll send the order form and the invoice allocation note in the same email, and I'll hold the March 1 start date on our side.
